units.title: Forecast: rain clearing, turning colder
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Light rain this morning clearing eastwards by early afternoon, with sunny spells following from the west. Wind veering south-westerly, then westerly 3 to 4. Maximum 8 C. Tonight: clear and cold with a widespread frost inland, minimum minus 1 C at Brackwater, 3 C on the coast. Outlook for the coming days: settled, dry and cold, with light winds and frost each night.

units.title: Service update: normal timetable
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. All sailings on the Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver route are operating to the normal timetable today. Passengers are advised that there may be frost on ramps and walkways from tomorrow morning; please use the handrails. Next month's timetable is now available at terminals and online, with night sailings unchanged from the current pattern.

units.title: Gilliver feeder: incident closed
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. The Gilliver coastal feeder has now run for more than 24 hours without interruption following completion of our insulator replacement programme. We are closing the incident and returning to normal monitoring. A full report on the recent faults will be shared with the regulator. Customers can still claim goodwill payments under the revised eight-hour threshold until the end of next month.

units.title: Hazard: floating timber, Gilliver approach
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Floating timber has been reported in the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm: several lengths of roundwood, three to five metres long, drifting with the tidal stream. The source has not been confirmed. Mariners, particularly small craft and creel boats, should keep a good lookout, reduce speed and report positions to Gilliver harbour office. Do not attempt to recover large timber alongside.

units.title: Roads: works completed and reopenings
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. Junction improvement works at the Brackwater junction on the A-road are complete and the temporary traffic lights have been removed. Mill Lane in Tollinby has reopened following flooding. The A-road at the Brackwater dip is fully open. We thank road users for their patience. Feedback on the new junction layout can be given through the council's online form.

units.title: Flood alert removed: Brackwater Burn
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office, with the river authority. The flood alert for the Brackwater Burn has been removed. River levels peaked yesterday evening just below the road bridge deck and are now falling steadily. Footpaths near the burn may remain wet and muddy for several days, and some footbridges in Brackwater Woods remain closed for inspection.

units.title: Waste collections: back to normal
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. All catch-up recycling rounds have now been completed, including the Gilliver front this morning. Collections return to their normal days from next week. Bulky waste collections, suspended during the recent disruption, will resume on Monday. We are grateful to residents who left boxes out and to those who wrote to tell us so.

units.title: Tides: spring tides this week
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound tides. High water Port Ammet 06:58 and 19:16; Gilliver 07:14 and 19:32. Spring tides over the next four days, with high waters around 0.4 m above average and correspondingly low low waters. Take care on slipways and foreshores, where weed exposed at low water may be slippery with frost. Sea state smooth to slight in the Sound.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby, next week
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Planned maintenance on the Tollinby town network next Wednesday between 09:00 and 13:00 will require a short interruption to supply for around 180 properties on Market Street, Church Street and Mill Lane. Affected customers will receive a letter. This work is unrelated to the recent faults on the Gilliver coastal feeder.

units.title: Gilliver: floating timber
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. Following a Coastguard notice about floating timber between Gilliver and Kittering Holm, our vessels will approach Gilliver at reduced speed tonight with an additional lookout posted. Passengers may notice a slightly longer crossing time on the 18:20 and 21:40 sailings. There is no risk to passengers. We thank the Gilliver harbour office for its assistance.

units.title: Brackwater: discoloured tap water
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council, on behalf of the water company. Some customers in Brackwater may notice discoloured tap water following high flows at the treatment works. The water is safe to drink. Run your cold kitchen tap for a few minutes until it clears. If it has not cleared within an hour, please contact the water company. Avoid washing white laundry until the water runs clear.

units.title: River mouths: debris notice cancelled
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Our notice of yesterday concerning debris near river and burn mouths, including the Port Ammet harbour entrance, is cancelled; most debris has grounded or been recovered. The separate notice concerning floating timber between Gilliver and Kittering Holm remains in force until further notice.

units.title: Outlook: cold, clear and calm
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound Met Office, extended outlook. High pressure builds over the Sound from tomorrow, bringing several days of dry, cold and calm weather. Winds light and variable. Frost each night, severe in sheltered inland spots, with temperatures down to minus 4 C around Brackwater. Some freezing fog possible at dawn in valleys, but clear on the coast. Long, still, starry nights.

units.title: Teenager says he was the 'figure' on Gilliver slipway on one foggy night
units.author: courier
units.text: A Gilliver teenager has admitted that he stood at the end of the village's ferry slipway in fog on one night earlier this month as a dare, accounting for one of several reports of an unidentified person on slipways in the Sound. The 17-year-old posted an apology on a local internet forum on Tuesday night. He is not being named.

units.author: courier
units.text: In his post, the teenager said he had worn a long coat belonging to his grandfather and stood on the slip for about ten minutes after a village hall disco on the night of the 7th. 'I only did it once,' he wrote. He said he had not been on the Gilliver slipway on the earlier night reported by a ferry crew, and had never been to the Lisle slip at night.

units.author: courier
units.text: Gilliver's harbourmaster confirmed that one report, logged by a relief ferry crew on the night of the 7th, had been 'accounted for' and that she had spoken to the young person and his family. 'He has apologised and the matter is closed,' she said. She asked the public to leave the family alone. She declined to comment on the other reports.

units.author: courier
units.text: The first report, on the night of the 4th, came from the crew of a night ferry who said they hailed a person standing at the water's edge of the Gilliver slipway twice and received no answer. A member of that crew said this week that she stood by her account and that the person she saw was considerably taller than the teenager. A separate sighting at Lisle on the 10th remains unexplained.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines, which reduced its night crossings for several days after the reports and has since fitted permanent extra lighting, said it 'welcomed the young man's honesty' and had no further comment. Slipways in the Sound remain closed to the public after dark under harbour byelaws.

units.title: Brackwater junction works finish two weeks late
units.author: courier
units.text: Roadworks at the Brackwater junction on the A-road were completed yesterday, two weeks behind schedule, and the temporary traffic lights that drivers had come to dread have been removed. The council said the delay was caused by the discovery of an old water main and by recent power interruptions, which had left the temporary lights dark on several nights.

units.author: courier
units.text: The new layout includes a dedicated right-turn lane for traffic heading towards Brackwater village. Some regular drivers have already complained that the lane is too short for vans and lorries. 'It fits one car, and that's on a good day,' one delivery driver told the Courier. The council said it would 'monitor the junction in operation'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The A-road dip near Brackwater, which flooded during this week's heavy rain, has fully reopened after pumping. The Tollinby school bus returned to its normal route yesterday afternoon. Mill Lane in Tollinby also reopened yesterday after floodwater receded.

units.title: Online 'portfolio' list for island buyer does not match registry
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: A list circulating online this week, which claimed to show remote properties owned by Ardent Vale Holdings alongside Kittering Holm, does not match public registry records, according to two planning and property consultants who examined it at the Journal's request. The list named a former radar station, a quarry, a sea fort and a valley estate.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: None of the reference numbers on the list corresponds to any format used by the registry. At least one of the properties, the former radar station, was bought at auction last spring by a conservation charity, whose ownership is a matter of public record. Another was listed with a purchase date earlier than the incorporation of Ardent Vale Holdings itself.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: 'Nominee companies do make ownership hard to trace, which is exactly why lists like this spread,' said one consultant. 'But a list that can't be checked isn't evidence of anything except that someone typed it.' The person who first posted the list said he had received it from a correspondent and was rechecking it.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Ardent Vale bought Kittering Holm through an intermediary about eighteen months ago. Its accounts, filed in Halvard, describe its business as 'the long-term holding of land and property' and show no other property in the Marrow Sound region. They are silent on holdings elsewhere.

units.title: Ardent Vale statement on 'wider portfolio' raises fresh questions
units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings, the owner of Kittering Holm, has issued a statement about what it called 'recent inaccurate reports of our wider portfolio', following the circulation online of a list of remote properties said to belong to the company. In the statement, sent to the Courier and to local contacts this morning, the company said it 'does not hold, and has never held, the properties named'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The same statement went on to say that 'those sites referred to which are associated with our partners are managed separately and are not part of our current plans'. Asked by the Courier to explain how sites it had never held could be associated with its partners, and who those partners were, the company issued a second note around two hours later.

units.author: courier
units.text: The clarification said that 'partners' should be read as 'unrelated third parties' and that Ardent Vale 'has no partners in the Marrow Sound'. It added that the company remained 'a patient, responsible owner with a long-term vision for the Holm' and looked forward to 'sharing more in due course'. It did not say what it would share or when.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company has previously said it had 'no plans to announce at this time'. Registry experts told the Courier that the list which prompted the statement did not match public records and appeared to be unreliable. The Courier has not published the list and does not regard it as accurate.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services, the contractor clearing the island, said it had no comment on the owner's other affairs. The clearance contract ends this week. The Courier has asked both companies when the crew working on the island will return to the mainland, and whether Ardent Vale intends to visit the site after the work is complete.

units.title: The stairwell that kept a tower block awake
units.author: weypost
units.text: For most of this month, residents of Dellow Court have been arguing, online and in the lift, about footsteps. Several said they heard someone on the stairs between the sixth and eighth floors when nobody was there, often while the stairwell lights were out. The lights, everyone now agrees, were a failed timer relay. The footsteps are less settled.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents have tried hard to explain them. A disused drinks chiller in the eighth-floor bin store was checked this week and found to be unplugged. A personal trainer on the tenth floor has offered his early-morning treadmill as a possible cause, and has put a thick mat beneath it. A railway signalling technician who has studied the timings says that most reports came between midnight and three, when nobody is running.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A building acoustics consultant who lives nearby said that concrete towers carry sound in strange ways and that 'footsteps' are among the commonest complaints in high-rise housing. 'Two floors up and one riser over can sound like right behind you,' she said. One family moved out of the building this month; another resident, in her seventies, says she still hears the steps in daylight.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association has started a thread on its message board for 'something nice', which this week included a late rose, a driving test and a drawing of the docks' cranes as herons, now pinned in the lift. 'It's a maintenance issue, which is still an issue,' said the association's secretary. 'But we're still neighbours.'

units.title: Villages gather winter parcels for island crew
units.author: courier
units.text: Residents of Lisle, Gilliver and Tollinby are collecting winter parcels for the crew clearing Kittering Holm, in a gesture organisers compare to the parcels once sent to lighthouse keepers. The Lisle Women's Institute has offered to assemble the parcels, which so far include socks, a hand-knitted scarf, shortbread, paperbacks and twenty-six cards made by a Tollinby primary class.

units.author: courier
units.text: 'We don't know the crew, and that isn't really the point,' said the institute's organiser, a retired Lisle headteacher. 'They're working out there in the dark through the worst of the weather, and people here wanted to do something.' A Port Ammet florist is making lavender bags to go in with the socks.

units.author: courier
units.text: It is not yet clear how the parcels will reach the island, which is served by a private supply boat. Grieve Land Services said it would 'look into' forwarding them. The organisers said they would hold on to everything until they heard, and that the cards, at least, would keep.

units.title: Rain clears: live updates
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:20 ST. Good morning. Light rain is clearing from the west and the Met Office expects a dry afternoon, followed by a cold, clear night with frost inland. The flood alert for the Brackwater Burn is expected to be lifted this morning. All ferries are running normally.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:40 ST. The Coastguard has issued a hazard notice for floating timber in the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm. Several lengths of roundwood have been reported drifting with the tide. The source hasn't been confirmed. Creel boats are being asked to keep a sharp lookout.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:30 ST. Ardent Vale, the owner of Kittering Holm, has issued a statement denying that it owns properties named in a list circulating online. A second note clarifying the first followed later in the morning. The Courier has both statements in full. Grieve Land Services says it has no comment.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:50 ST. The sun is out over Port Ammet for the first time in three days. Brackwater residents are being advised to run their cold taps if water is discoloured after high flows at the treatment works. Sound Power has closed its incident on the Gilliver feeder after more than a day without interruption.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:05 ST. Sound Lines says its vessels will approach Gilliver at reduced speed tonight with an extra lookout because of the floating timber. A creel fisherman who got close to one length this afternoon told us it was birch with clean cuts at both ends, and that it could have come from any timber yard along a flooded burn.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:30 ST. Temperatures are falling quickly under clear skies: 4 C at Carrow Point and 2 C at Brackwater already. Gritters are out on the A-road and the ridge road. Listeners in Gilliver say the island's camp lights are unusually sharp tonight across the water.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 22:10 ST. Last update from the news desk tonight. Frost is forming on untreated roads and pavements across the Sound; take care if you're out. The settled, cold spell is expected to last for several days. The overnight show is on air now with your calls.

units.title: Spares on the next boat
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a quick one. The yard is sending a box of spare chains and two files out on tomorrow's boat as standard for the last week, whether you've asked or not. They do it on every job of this length, because chains go fastest at the end. If you don't need them, send them back unopened with the empties and they won't be charged. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Tomorrow's boat
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper has confirmed he'll go out at noon tomorrow, rain or no rain. The forecast wind stays moderate, so he expects no trouble landing. He'll bring the spares, the usual supplies and the newspapers, and he'll take back any empty drums you leave by the landing. That's all for today. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry, I forgot to say. If he asks about Mum, she's fine, she had her check-up and the doctor said her blood pressure is 'boringly normal', which she was very pleased about. He worries about her more than he says. Please tell him that too, if you have time. I'm sorry for the second email. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: p.s. forgot to say, the dog ate one of mum's physio socks, the grippy kind with the rubber dots, and has been very quiet and pleased with himself all evening. the vet says it'll come out the usual way. I've told mum it was 'lost in the wash'. don't tell her. love, S x

units.title: Notice: leaver processed
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Notice reference GLS-KH-LVR. A crew member has been recorded as having left the Kittering Holm contract. The day rate for this worker has ceased from the recorded date of departure. Any wages due to the worker up to that date remain payable under the usual terms. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Contract close: statement schedule
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Notice reference GLS-KH-CLS. The final statement for the Kittering Holm contract will be issued after contract close, based on the verified tree count and the day-rate register. Payment will be made within ten working days of the statement date. Queries should be raised through your operations contact. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Five tips for winter driving
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear policyholder, frosty mornings are on the way! Here are five tips from Lyle Mutual: clear all windows fully before setting off; check tyre tread and pressure; keep a blanket and a torch in the car; leave extra stopping distance; and tell someone your route on longer journeys. Your policy LM-VH-55831 includes breakdown cover as standard. Lyle Mutual: peace of mind, whatever the weather.

units.title: The last few days: the plan
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, with the rain clearing, here's the plan as it stands. 1. The last working day is contract day 30. Work stops at dusk. 2. The crew boat collects everyone the morning after; I'll confirm the time by day 29. 3. The final count is taken from the usual figures on the evening of day 30. 4. Please keep the whole crew on site until the boat arrives, so nobody tries to make their own way. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Cosy camp reads (and frosty-night essentials!)
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello from Camp Supply! The rain's moving off and the frosts are moving in, so it's time to get cosy! Our team's favourite tips: line your boots with newspaper overnight, keep a flask by the bed, and a lantern on the windowsill makes any camp feel like home! This week only: thermal socks three for two, and 10% off hot water bottles! Stay warm out there! The Camp Supply team

units.title: Travel home for the crew
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, travel home is sorted at our end. The crew boat lands at Gilliver, where a minibus will take everyone to the Port Ammet ferry terminal, and Grieve has booked foot passenger tickets on the first sailing after. Anyone going on to Weyhaven or Tollinby will be given a rail warrant. Could you check the crew have photo ID with them for the warrants? Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A community update from Ardent Vale
units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: Dear neighbours and partners, Ardent Vale is aware of recent inaccurate reports of our wider portfolio. We wish to be clear: Ardent Vale does not hold, and has never held, the properties named in material circulating online. Our interest in the Marrow Sound is Kittering Holm, which we steward with patience and respect. Those sites referred to which are associated with our partners are managed separately and are not part of our current plans. Warm regards, Community Information, Ardent Vale

units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: A clarification to this morning's community update. Where our note referred to 'partners', this should be read as referring to unrelated third parties. Ardent Vale has no partners in the Marrow Sound. We remain a patient, responsible owner with a long-term vision for the Holm, rooted in respect for the Sound and its communities, and we look forward to sharing more in due course. Warm regards, Community Information, Ardent Vale

units.title: The client's statement
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, you may have had the client's community update in your inbox this morning, and a second one after it. You don't need to do anything with either. If the crew have heard about it through the papers, please reassure them it has nothing to do with our work. The job is the job, and it's nearly done. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Ardent Vale's statement, and one question
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. You'll probably have seen Ardent Vale's two notes this morning. I asked them what 'managed separately' meant and got the second note by way of an answer, which I suspect you'll find as clear as I did. I've asked Grieve when the crew are due back. I'd like to ask you one thing only, entirely off the record: has anyone told you when you're being collected? Kind regards, Nell

units.title: Boat tomorrow
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the supply boat goes out tomorrow at noon as normal. The skipper has been told about the timber in the channel and will come in slowly. He'd like the landing kept clear of any logs, please, as he doesn't want anything rolling into the water while he's alongside. He'll take back the empties and any kit you've finished with. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Handover walk
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the client's agent will walk the island after handover. They haven't given us a date yet, and they've said they don't need anyone from the crew there. It won't affect your payment, which is based on the verified count as normal. If anything has been damaged on site, a hut, a path, anything, just note it on the demob list so it doesn't come as a surprise. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Wages before close
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I'm sorry to come back to this. Payroll still shows crew wages outstanding on your side. If it's settled before contract day 30, the final payment goes through without any delay. If it isn't, head office will hold the final payment until it is, and I won't be able to change that. Let me know if there's anything I can do from here. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Timber in the water
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello again, briefly. The Coastguard has reported cut timber drifting between Gilliver and the island. A fisherman told Sound FM it could have come from any yard on a flooded burn, which seems likely to me. I've asked Grieve whether any timber has gone into the water from the Holm, mainly so that we don't print something unfair. If it's nothing, I'd be glad simply to know that. Nell

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: A short update on the parcels, since I mentioned them. Grieve's office said they would 'look into' forwarding them. The Lisle Women's Institute will hold onto everything until they hear. There are now twenty-six cards from a Tollinby class, mostly of trees, one of a dog. I'm told they will keep. I thought you'd like to know people are thinking of you. Nell

units.title: Today
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, today's figure has come through to head office, thank you. The rain has gone and the Met Office has cold, calm, dry weather for the rest of the contract, so the next three days should be long ones. Please make sure everyone gets proper rest tonight. Frost on the ground from tomorrow, so mind the slopes in the morning. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: frost tomorrow
units.author: sam
units.text: hi. the rain's stopped here and the sky's gone that hard clear blue, so it's going to freeze. mum has put the dog's coat on him indoors 'to get him used to it'. he's lying under the table in it looking betrayed. the kid wants to know if there's snow on your island. I said islands don't get snow, which I think is wrong. the paper's full of a company statement nobody understands. love, S x

units.title: The canal went down
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry, me again. Please tell Tomas the canal has gone down and the car is back outside the flat. Tell him I'm fine. I've been reading the Evening Post and it says the work finishes in three days. Is he sleeping? He gets a sort of crease between his eyes when he isn't, if you've noticed it. I'm sorry, I know that's a strange thing to tell you. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: me again. I read the whole courier tonight. the slipway thing was a kid, which was a relief, except the ferry woman says it wasn't the same kid, or not a kid at all. and there are logs floating in the sea near you, and the company says it doesn't own things and then says it does, sort of. I know none of that is your job. I just want you on that boat. love, S x

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: One more thing, and then I'll stop. When the boat comes, will you make sure he gets on it? He always stays behind to help someone carry something, he did it at every school trip and every wedding. Tell him I said to go first for once. Thank you. I'm sorry for all these emails. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: three more days. mum's counting them on the kitchen calendar with a pen, crossing them off like it's advent. the dog has taken his coat off by himself and hidden it. that's all. sleep well. keep warm. love, S x

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk: a correction, against my own position. I have now examined the camp's wage ledger (Society holdings, MS 14a), which is separate from the clerk's diary and was kept by the company's agent in Port Ammet, not by the clerk. It shows every man on the roster paid in full to his last day, with no disputes noted and no deductions beyond boots and a lost axe. My pay-dispute theory is not supported. I withdraw it.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Talk: thank you, and well done; it isn't easy to withdraw a theory in public. I've added the ledger to the article's sources. That leaves the camp's departure without a recorded cause. I've written 'reason not recorded' in the infobox rather than anything more interesting. [citation needed: anything at all from the company's side]

units.title: Penhallow camp diary: December 1894, further entries
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 17th. Fair, hard frost. Tally 52, the men working only the near lines by Mr Coad's leave. The far lines left standing, about two acres. Oil account 3 gall. since Thursday. Treloar back at work. A fox in the stores at night, or so the cook says, though nothing taken. Roster 15. All in by the lamps, and the lamps up till morning.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec. 19th. Calm and very still, no wind at all, which the men remark upon. No felling; Mr Coad gone across to Gilliver on the boat to see the agent, returning Saturday. Men at the saw-pit in the morning and in the bunkhouse after noon. I have made up the tallies to date and they are correct. Psalm 4 read at supper. 'I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep.'

units.title: Carrow Point logbook: late February (excerpt)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Feb. 24th. 00:00 Light exhibited, burning well. Wind NW 3, clear, hard frost. 01:00 Lamp trimmed. Asst. Keeper Hosking arrived by the afternoon boat to replace Moyle, who leaves Thursday. Showed him the watch. 02:00 Remarks: Hosking asked who the walkers were on the shore road. I said they were people from the village. 03:00 Clear. 04:00 Light burning well.

units.title: Arnell field notebook: Kittering Holm, eighth day (last)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Eighth day. Clear, still, cold. Intended a final ridge transect; Jory arrived at noon instead of eight and said we must be off by two, the weather 'turning', though the glass was steady and the sky without a cloud. I argued and lost. Packed the presses. Summary for the survey: birds 31 species; mammals: otter, mice, no rabbit, no deer. Left the island at a quarter to two. Jory rowed very fast.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 6. Recommendation. The Holm ridge is technically suitable for a relay station, with clear sightlines to Carrow Point and Lisle and adequate ground for foundations. The estimated capital cost is within the Board's provision. Nevertheless the undersigned recommends against proceeding, for reasons of staffing, as set out at section 4. An automated light at Lisle would serve the same approach at lower running cost. R. Talbot, CEng.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 14, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewee: Mrs M. R., born 1902, Gilliver. Q: Do you remember the timber men coming back from the Holm? A: That was before my time, but my mother said they came back at Christmas with all their money and spent it at the Anchor. Q: Were they frightened? A: Frightened? They were drunk. [laughs] No, she said they were quiet. Quiet men. They wouldn't sit with their backs to the window.

units.title: 'From Our Gilliver Correspondent', 1896: the Holm let
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: [Editor's note, G. Faulds: from the column of 14 March 1896, page 6.] We hear that the timber lease on the Holm will not be renewed this year, the gentlemen of the company having found the work 'unprofitable at the distance'. The stands upon the north end remain uncut. Our boatmen report that the old huts have already fallen in, and that nobody has thought it worth the trouble to bring the iron back.

units.title: Courier, 1923: lady naturalist returns from the Holm
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: [Editor's note: from page 4, 22 September 1923. The paper misspells her name throughout; the society's copy of her notebook confirms 'Arnell'.] Miss Arnold, the lady naturalist, returned to Gilliver on Thursday after a week's survey of the birds and beasts of Kittering Holm. She reports the island 'most interesting' and 'curiously quiet', and expresses her gratitude to Mr Jory, the boatman, for his care of her party.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue note, LB-2611. The recordist has since been in touch and has asked that the entry remain as it is: 'ends abruptly'. At his request the words 'recordist unavailable' have been removed. The final eleven seconds have still not been reviewed by the catalogue, and the recordist has asked that they not be. That request is recorded here and will be respected.

units.title: Rendle diary: December 1936, continued
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Dec 12 1936. Frost and dead calm, the Sound like glass. Too still Jack says. Did not go out, mended pots in the shed. The curing station roof has come off on the Holm side, you can see the rafters from the front. Old Penrose says leave it be. Mother lit her lamp at four. Ours and every house on the front, you could see them all lit from the quay.

units.title: LB-0067: Brackwater woods, night ambience, 1983 (cassette transfer)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: Catalogue no. LB-0067. Date: October 1983 (cassette J-card). Location: Brackwater Woods, 'the track above the reservoir'. Source: consumer cassette, donated by the recordist's daughter. Duration: 00:22:40. Content: tawny owls, wind, distant traffic, and at 00:14:10 four percussive events at irregular intervals, unattributed. The recordist's voice says 'that'll be the deer' and the tape stops shortly after.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Nobody dumps logs in the sea, Gil. That's money floating off. A good birch butt is worth something to someone, even round here. If they've come off a yard it's because the burn took them, simple as. I'd be down there with a boat hook if I had a boat.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: The gum man! I know the gum man, he's lovely, he holds the door for me and tells me what the bus is doing. If he says 'which other one' then I'm choosing to believe there was never another one. That's not science. That's just me, very tired, with a cake bar.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: 'Never held' and 'managed separately' in one statement isn't a cover-up, it's a press office with two writers and no editor. I've read worse from the council, and from our own station, more than once. The clarification made it worse, which is the usual way of these things. Source for all of this: years of reading press releases at 3am.
